Following up on @bherdm's comment in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101036#issuecomment-2568642125

> Building the engine is working fine on macOS, but it seems to have broken building the Android export template. Here's the error I'm getting:
> 
> ```
> scons: Reading SConscript files ...
> Using custom revision: OUYA
> Godot Android!!!!! (armv7) (with neon)
> Using NDK unified headers
> NameError: global name 'LooseVersion' is not defined:
>   File "/Users/bherdm/GitHub/godot/SConstruct", line 296:
>     detect.configure(env)
>   File "./platform/android/detect.py", line 259:
>     if ndk_version != None and LooseVersion(ndk_version) >= LooseVersion("15.0.4075724"):
> ```
> 
> I have been using NDK 17.2.4988734.

Indeed I had missed some `LooseVersion`s in the Android fix, should now be fixed in 64a9c5ac.

> Also, and maybe interestingly, this did break building the engine using Windows VS2015 x64 Native, but it's still working in x64 2022 and VS2015 x64 x86 Cross Tools.

What error are you getting?

There should be no change affecting Visual Studio builds in this PR so far. I wanted to specify an explicit C++ standard but it's not possible with old MSVC, and new versions only support explicit C++14 or later. So there should be no impact compared to the current `2.1` branch.

Added another fix for a Python 3 issue when writing to text files, which would prevent me from building the Android APK as the AndroidManifest.xml was 0 bytes. With this fix I can generate an APK fine using NDK r17c and Temurin OpenJDK 8.

Did some testing for the Web platform too, it took me a while to find a version of Emscripten that works.

It seems like the `2.1` branch was still using asm.js, and when Emscripten moved to llvm-upstream in 1.39.0, they dropped support for that. So to compile successfully one needs to use a 1.38.x version (and it seems like only 1.38.33 to 1.38.48 are qavailable, older versions were hosted by Mozilla and are now dead links), or 1.39.x with the `-fastcomp` option while it's supported, so on emsdk:

```
git checkout 1.39.1  # To have old tagged versions and compatible install scripts.
./emsdk install 1.38.48
./emsdk activate 1.38.48
source emsdk_env.sh
```

or likewise with `1.39.1-fastcomp`.

The build succeeds, but I couldn't get a 2.1 project to run on modern browsers with my build. There's a ton of errors in the console. I tested with 2.1.6 export templates and it fails similarly, so I assume it's just that browsers don't support what we were using back then anymore. My archiving work stops here for now :)

I haven't reviewed the code, but I just tested building the editor on Ubuntu 22.04 with GCC 11.4 and it worked great! I played a nice little game of minesweeper from the template on the asset library :-)

If I don't do `git clean -dfx` before, I get a build error on VS 2022 x64 (using its native command prompt):

```
[ 39%] Compiling ==> core\version_hash.gen.cpp
version_hash.gen.cpp
core\version_hash.gen.cpp(36): error C4430: missing type specifier - int assumed. Note: C++ does not support default-int
core\version_hash.gen.cpp(36): error C2146: syntax error: missing ';' before identifier 'VERSION_TIMESTAMP'
core\version_hash.gen.cpp(36): error C2059: syntax error: '='
scons: *** [core\version_hash.gen.windows.tools.64.obj] Error 2
```

Otherwise, it builds successfully even with `-j32` (in only 25 seconds on an i9-13900K). A release export template also compiles and runs successfully. Minilens runs correctly from the editor.

With `tools=no target=release`, I get a build error though:

```
[ 10%] Compiling ==> thirdparty\libmpcdec\mpc_bits_reader.c
mpc_bits_reader.c
thirdparty\libmpcdec\mpc_bits_reader.c(101): error C2365: 'log2': redefinition; previous definition was 'function'
thirdparty\libmpcdec\mpc_bits_reader.c(139): error C2109: subscript requires array or pointer type
thirdparty\libmpcdec\mpc_bits_reader.c(140): error C2109: subscript requires array or pointer type
thirdparty\libmpcdec\mpc_bits_reader.c(140): error C2198: 'mpc_uint32_t mpc_bits_read(mpc_bits_reader *,const unsigned int)': too few arguments for call
scons: *** [thirdparty\libmpcdec\mpc_bits_reader.windows.opt.64.obj] Error 2
scons: building terminated because of errors.
```

> The build succeeds, but I couldn't get a 2.1 project to run on modern browsers with my build. There's a ton of errors in the console. I tested with 2.1.6 export templates and it fails similarly, so I assume it's just that browsers don't support what we were using back then anymore. My archiving work stops here for now :)

It's strange, considering many other asm.js-based projects like [QuakeJS](http://www.quakejs.com) still run in modern Firefox and Chromium today.

Hiya all,  I've figured out how to make godot 2.1.6 works on modern web browser when building a custom export template with help of Scons 2.5.1, Emscripten 1.38.48, and python 2.7.13.
1.
I used the following CMD command on Windows 11:
```
platform=javascript target=release tools=no disable_3d=yes disable_advanced_gui=yes builtin_openssl=no module_openssl_enabled=no -j1
```
I had to rip off openssl due to the limited command line length on Windows 11 when linking a static library.
2.
I followed the official guide  where it says: 

>[...] This can be done in the export GUI, using the **“Custom Package” option. There’s no need to copy the templates in this case — you can simply reference the resulting files in your Godot source folder**, [...].

> referenced: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/2.1/development/compiling/compiling_for_web.html.

3.
The export worked on Chrome. Well, almost... The **godot.javascript.opt.exe.html** ignored the **data.pck** and just take the following files:
**godot.javascript.opt.exe.asm.js
godot.javascript.opt.exe.html.mem
godot.javascript.opt.exe.js**

**Workaround 1**: I took borrow the .html file of the official export template (javascript.release.zip file) and within that file I just went to the lines of code where the **asm.js**, the **html.mem** and the **.js** files where referenced and I just renamed those files. You can check at the following repository: https://minec-c.github.io/export216x64pj1/godotapk2/godot.javascript.opt.exe.html

**Workaround 2**:
Within the godot.javascript.opt.exe.asm.js file, I replaced the 1th line of code by the 2th line:
```
_emscripten_get_num_gamepads(){return JSEvents.lastGamepadState.length}
_emscripten_get_num_gamepads(){return 0}
```

Finally revisiting this to get it merged.
So I'm booting Windows for the first time in 6 months 😅

We fixed that issue for 4.0 in #53860 but I don't intend to backport this to `2.1`. So when switching branches the `.gen.cpp` files need to be deleted (or the whole repo cleaned, which is better IMO when switching to such an old branch).

@minec-c Great finds, thanks!

For the build command, I got it to compile successfully with Python 3, SCons 3.1.2 and Emscripten 1.38.48 with just `scons p=javascript tools=no target=release`. I used the PowerShell terminal.

For the files naming issue, there's some post-processing necessary on the generated files in `2.1`, which you can follow here:
https://github.com/GodotBuilder/godot-builds/blob/513e409eb4d722f6d98b2bec59058a369ba538c6/.travis.yml#L200-L210

It's also described in the docs for 2.1 but it seems somewhat outdated: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/2.1/development/compiling/compiling_for_web.html#building-export-templates
The above Travis script is what was used to build official releases for 2.1.

> Workaround 2:
> Within the godot.javascript.opt.exe.asm.js file, I replaced the 1th line of code by the 2th line:
> ```
> _emscripten_get_num_gamepads(){return JSEvents.lastGamepadState.length}
> _emscripten_get_num_gamepads(){return 0}
> ```

I confirm that this function causes an error and replacing it with `0` fixes it. Note that it's in the main `godot.js` file, not `godot.asm.js`. It's caused by this Emscripten compat breakage: https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/issues/7840

This was fixed in Godot 3.0 by #25149, so I'm cherry-picking it. That seems to do the trick at least as long as a gamepad isn't connected.

With a gamepad connected I get errors again. I'd say solving gamepad support for the old `2.1` branch is outside the scope of this PR (it's also broken in the current `2.1` HEAD). Eventually the whole Emscripten gamepad API was dropped in #45079 to replace it with a custom one. But that's way too big to backport to `2.1` just for the sake of preservation, at least I'm not doing it ;)

I found another fix for the Emscripten gamepad handling code that fixes this: #21588.

With this cherry-picked, gamepad support seems to work, including hotplugging (only tested in Firefox and Chromium).

In Chromium it seems to work just fine.
In Firefox, the mappings are partially wrong, I believe that's something that was addressed by #45079 but again this is out of scope of this attempt at making 2.1 compile on modern toolchains. On a knockoff PS3 controller, I noticed that the D-pad doesn't seem to work and the face buttons are flipped, but a demo like the 2D platformer is playable.
